modelSettings.title: Model settings
modelSettings.description: Recommended values are based on this model and system memory. Review them before applying.
modelSettings.estimatedMemoryTooltip: The combined model, KV cache, and runtime buffer calculated from downloaded metadata and the current context setting. Actual usage may vary by runtime and system state.
modelSettings.automaticSetupGgufTooltip:
Vyact automatic runtime settings (GGUF)
GPU offload: Automatic
Memory fitting: Automatic
Concurrent generation: 1
Flash Attention: Automatic
Prompt cache: Enabled
RoPE, mmap, KV GPU offload: llama.cpp defaults
modelSettings.automaticSetupMlxTooltip:
Vyact automatic runtime settings (MLX)
Metal execution: Managed by the MLX runtime
Prompt cache (APC): Enabled
Batch, threads, and memory management: MLX defaults
modelSettings.contextTooltip: The maximum amount of conversation and document text the model can consider at once. Large values can use substantial memory and slow down your computer. Even if set to the model’s maximum, lower it to suit the conversation and document length you need and the memory available on your computer.
modelSettings.contextRangeError: Enter a context window between {{min}} and {{max}} tokens.
modelSettings.maxOutputTooltip:
Leave empty for Auto.
Auto: reserves 40% of the space left after required input for output.
Number: sets an output cap, adjusted to fit the remaining space.
modelSettings.historyTokenBudgetTooltip:
Leave empty for Auto.
Auto: after reserving output, splits the rest between material (75%) and history (25%), redistributing unused space.
Number: includes recent messages up to the cap. 0 excludes history.
modelSettings.temperatureTooltip: Controls randomness. Lower values are more consistent and factual; higher values are more varied and creative. 0.2 is a safe general-purpose value.
modelSettings.topKTooltip: Limits each next-token choice to the K most likely candidates. Leave it at the model default unless you understand sampling controls.
modelSettings.topPTooltip: Chooses from the smallest group of likely tokens whose combined probability reaches this value. Leave it at the model default for normal use.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitOffHelp: Off · Recommended. llama.cpp automatically fits the model to available GPU memory for the more stable setup.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitOnHelp: On · Uses the values below as a fixed split ratio. Automatic memory fitting is limited and an unsuitable split may fail to load.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitTooltip: OFF leaves tensor allocation to llama.cpp --fit and is the safer default. ON sends a manual --tensor-split percentage for each GPU; the total must be 100%.
modelSettings.gpuAllocationHelp: Estimated from each compatible GPU's VRAM ratio. Adjust only when balancing multiple GPUs.
modelSettings.gpuAllocationTooltip: Each value is a llama.cpp tensor split percentage with up to two decimal places, and the total must be 100%. It is not a hard VRAM usage limit.
modelSettings.gpuSplitInvalid: Set the GPU split percentages to a total of 100%.
modelSettings.gpuSplitCapacityWarning: At this ratio, GPU {{index}} may receive about {{required}}, exceeding its {{capacity}} VRAM. Actual llama.cpp allocation may differ, but the model may fail to load. Use the recommended ratio or turn off manual splitting.
modelSettings.mtpAccelerationHelp: Speeds up generation with the model's MTP predictor. Turn it off to use KV cache quantization.
modelSettings.omlxMtpAccelerationHelp: Uses the installed compatible external MTP draft through oMLX. Memory Cache remains enabled.
modelSettings.dflash2AccelerationHelp: DFlash2 is detected and enabled automatically for this model.
modelSettings.dflash2AccelerationTooltip: Runs a compatible DFlash2 draft through llama.cpp or oMLX. Only one speculative acceleration path is enabled at a time.
modelSettings.mtpAccelerationTooltip: MTP lets a compatible model predict several tokens ahead and can improve generation speed. It uses an additional predictor and cannot be combined with KV cache quantization in Vyact.
modelSettings.omlxMtpAccelerationTooltip: External MTP is used without SpecPrefill or native MTP. Only a compatible installed draft is selected.
modelSettings.cacheQuantizationHelp: Reduces cache memory use for larger contexts.
modelSettings.cacheQuantizationMtpHelp: Turn off MTP acceleration to enable KV cache quantization.
modelSettings.accelerationConflict: MTP acceleration and KV cache quantization cannot be enabled together.

mtpFailures.load_failed: MTP could not be loaded in this environment, so the model is running without it.
mtpFailures.out_of_memory: MTP could not be loaded because there was not enough memory, so the model is running without it.

modelSettings.performanceModeHelp: Adjusts llama.cpp batching for speed or lower memory use.
modelSettings.performanceModeTooltip: Auto uses Vyact's balanced defaults. Memory saving reduces temporary processing memory. Maximum performance uses larger batches and may require more memory.
modelSettings.cpuThreadsHelp: Limits llama.cpp CPU usage. Leave empty for automatic selection.
modelSettings.cpuThreadsTooltip: Sets how many CPU threads llama.cpp may use. A lower value reduces CPU load and heat but may slow generation. Leave empty unless you need to limit resource use.
modelSettings.kvCachePrecisionHelp: Q8 preserves more precision; Q4 uses less memory.
modelSettings.kvCachePrecisionTooltip: The KV cache stores the model's working memory for the current context. Q8 saves memory with a small quality tradeoff; Q4 saves more memory but can affect quality more. It cannot be used with MTP.
modelSettings.seedHelp: Leave empty for random. To reproduce results, enter any integer from 0 to 2,147,483,647 (for example, 42).
modelSettings.seedTooltip: A seed is the starting number for response randomness; the number itself does not improve performance or quality. You can use any integer from 0 to 2,147,483,647. Using the same seed makes results easier to reproduce when the input and all other settings are identical. Leave it empty to use a random seed for each request.

stockAnalysis.compareHelpChart: The colored line plots comparison closes on the left price axis. Main prices use the right axis. Units and ranges may differ.
stockAnalysis.compareHelpShift: −10 moves the entire comparison line 10 bars left: later comparison movements appear alongside earlier main-chart bars.
stockAnalysis.compareHelpPositive: +10 moves the entire comparison line 10 bars right: earlier comparison movements appear alongside later main-chart bars.

indicatorSettingHelp.bollinger: Period controls the moving average and standard deviation lookback; longer is smoother. Deviation multiplier widens or narrows the bands. Defaults: 20 bars, 2 deviations.
indicatorSettingHelp.ichimoku: Conversion, base and span B periods set high/low midpoint lookbacks. Displacement shifts leading spans forward and lagging close backward; it is not a forecast. Defaults: 9/26/52, shift 26 bars.
indicatorSettingHelp.sar: Acceleration step increases responsiveness at new trend extremes; maximum caps it and must be at least the step. Larger values may cause more reversals. Defaults: 0.02/0.2.
indicatorSettingHelp.envelope: Period sets the SMA lookback. Width is the percentage on EACH side: 5 means ±5%, a total span of 10% of the average. Defaults: 20 bars, ±2.5%.
indicatorSettingHelp.macd: Fast and slow periods set EMA lookbacks; fast must be shorter. Signal is the EMA period of MACD. Longer periods smooth more but lag. Defaults: 12/26/9 bars.
indicatorSettingHelp.rsi: Shorter periods make RSI more responsive. Lower/upper levels are guide lines only and do not change RSI values; lower must be smaller. Defaults: 14 bars, 30/70.
indicatorSettingHelp.adx: Period controls Wilder smoothing; longer is smoother. Trend level is a guide line only. Defaults: 14 bars, 25. Initial ADX requires roughly twice the period in history.
indicatorSettingHelp.obv: OBV has no period or level setting. It accumulates signed volume from zero at the beginning of loaded history, so the starting date affects its absolute value.
indicatorSettingHelp.fastStochastic: Period sets the high/low lookback for %K. Signal averages %K into %D; longer means smoother. Levels are guides only. Defaults: 14/3 bars, 20/80.
indicatorSettingHelp.slowStochastic: Period sets the raw %K lookback. Smoothing averages fast %K into slow %K; signal averages slow %K into %D. Longer means smoother and later. Levels are guides. Defaults: 14/3/3, 20/80.

bollinger.description: Moving-average midpoint with upper and lower bands based on population standard deviation. M, U and L denote middle, upper and lower.
bollinger.reading: Narrowing bands indicate lower volatility; widening bands indicate expansion. Touching a band alone does not imply reversal.

ichimoku.description: Five lines and a cloud show trend direction and possible support or resistance.
ichimoku.reading:
Lines: conversion tracks shorter-term movement; base tracks medium-term movement. Leading spans A/B form the cloud; the lagging span plots today’s close at an earlier position.
Bullish context: price above the cloud plus conversion crossing above base can suggest strengthening upward momentum.
Bearish context: price below the cloud plus conversion crossing below base can suggest strengthening downward momentum.
Inside the cloud: direction is less clear. A thicker cloud can represent a broader support/resistance zone, but can still break.
Caution: a crossing is not a standalone trade instruction. Forward clouds are not forecasts; the latest lagging segment is intentionally empty.

sar.description: A trend-following stop-and-reverse calculation with a configurable acceleration step and maximum.
sar.reading: Dots switching above price indicate a downward reversal and below price an upward reversal. Sideways markets can cause frequent switches.

envelope.description: A moving-average channel offset by a fixed percentage rather than standard deviation.
envelope.reading: Judge price distance from the average. Suitable width depends on symbol and interval; a breakout need not reverse.

macd.description: MACD is fast EMA minus slow EMA; signal is an EMA of MACD; histogram is their difference. Defaults: 12/26/9.
macd.reading: Read the zero line, signal crossings and histogram expansion together. Raw values use price units and are not directly comparable across stocks.

rsi.description: Wilder-smoothed relative gains and losses, scaled from 0 to 100. Default period 14, levels 30/70.
rsi.reading: High readings indicate strong upward momentum and low readings strong downward momentum. Overbought or oversold conditions can persist.

adx.description: ADX measures trend strength, not direction. +DI and −DI compare directional movement. Default period 14, level 25.
adx.reading: A rising ADX indicates strengthening trend. +DI above −DI favors upward direction. High ADX alone does not mean rising prices.

obv.description: Adds volume on higher closes, subtracts on lower closes and holds on unchanged closes. Starts at zero for the loaded history.
obv.reading: Look at trend and price divergence rather than absolute value. Results depend on history start; missing volume is not calculated.

fastStochastic.description: Fast %K locates the close in its recent high/low range; %D averages %K. Defaults: 14/3, levels 20/80.
fastStochastic.reading: Read crossings and threshold transitions with price trend. Fast responses also produce frequent noisy crossings.

slowStochastic.description: Smooths fast %K into slow %K, then averages it into %D. Defaults: 14/3/3, levels 20/80.
slowStochastic.reading: Smoother than fast stochastic, with fewer crossings but more delay. Threshold touches alone do not imply a reversal.
